Expect a table to match another

Source: R/expect.R
expect_table_equal.Rd

A testthat expectation built on diff_table(): it passes when every compared value is same. expected is the benchmark, as in testthat's expect_equal(object, expected), so the comparison is diff_table(expected, object, ...): object is cast to expected's types and its extra columns are dropped. Pass mode = "equal" to compare the two as peers instead.

Usage

expect_table_equal(
  object,
  expected,
  ...,
  rel_tol = sqrt(.Machine$double.eps),
  max_rows = 10L
)

Arguments

object

The table under test.

expected

The benchmark table.

...

Passed to diff_table(): mode, by, measures, tolerance, duplicates and so on.

rel_tol

The largest relative difference still counted as same, as in diff_table(). With duplicates = "aggregate", which compares exactly, it defaults to 0.

max_rows

The most records that differ shown in a failure.

Value

The diff_table() result, invisibly. On failure it is also attached to the failed expectation, as its "diff" attribute. NULL when the tables share no key, since there is no result.

Details

Unlike diff_table(), which is exact by default, the expectation allows a relative difference of sqrt(.Machine$double.eps) (about 1.5e-8), the default of testthat's expect_equal(): a value computed again rarely agrees with its stored copy to the last bit (0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3), and a test should not fail on that. It is still far below any difference a person would call real. Pass rel_tol = 0 for an exact comparison.

Duplicate keys are an error (dazdiff_error_duplicates), not a failure: pairing rows by arrival order is an assumption, and an assertion should not rest on one, so the test cannot be judged as written. The exception is a comparison with no measures, where the repeated rows are identical in every compared column and pairing them assumes nothing. Pass duplicates = "disambiguate" or "aggregate" to accept duplicates.

Tables that share no key – most often because object came back empty – fail the expectation. diff_table() refuses such a comparison as ill-formed, but under test it is an answer: the two tables differ in every row.

Examples

expected <- data.frame(id = 1:3, amount = c(10, 20, 30))
actual <- data.frame(id = 1:3, amount = c(10, 20, 30 + 1e-9))
expect_table_equal(actual, expected, tolerance = 1e-6)
